KAIST (Kim, Kang, Kim, Hwang); New York University (Yang, Ren); DeepAuto.ai (Hwang)

Evaluates (systematic investigation of cross-domain memory transfer for coding agents, RQ1-RQ3, comparing memory formats and MTL vs zero-shot, ReasoningBank, AgentKB); secondary: proposes an approach (MTL, labelled 'Ours')

Memory Transfer Learning (MTL): a unified memory pool from heterogeneous coding benchmarks, retrieved into the agent system prompt; four memory formats: Trajectory, Workflow, Summary, Insight (after ReasoningBank). Compared with ReasoningBank and AgentKB. No version

Memory items generated by an LLM from past agent trajectories: Trajectory (commands and observations), Workflow (goal + key actions), Summary (task summary + experience paragraph), Insight (title, one-sentence description, task-agnostic content). Top-3 memories (cosine similarity on text-embedding-3-small) inserted in the system prompt. No specification document

Offline: run agent on all benchmarks, LLM judge labels success/failure, generate memories with success/failure prompts, build pool excluding the test benchmark, embed. Online: for each task (for non-trajectory formats the model first writes a 4-5 sentence plan as query) retrieve N=3 memories, add to system prompt, agent solves task

Tasks: 6 benchmarks, up to 100 random tasks each. Configurations: zero-shot vs MTL with 4 memory formats (GPT-5-mini) and Insight for DeepSeek V3.2 and Qwen3-Coder-480B; vs ReasoningBank and AgentKB on 3 benchmarks; ablations on abstraction, pool size, domains, cross-model, retrieval. Baseline: zero-shot (no memory). Held constant: agent mini-swe-agent, model within comparison, N=3 memories, harbor evaluation, same LLM for memory generation/judge. Acceptance tests: benchmark evaluation protocols. Repetitions: three runs (Pass@3). Human intervention: none

MTL Insight best format: avg +3.7 points over zero-shot with GPT-5-mini (0.523 to 0.560), up to +8.3 on MLGym; +2.6 DeepSeek, +1.8 Qwen. Ranking Insight > Summary > Workflow > Trajectory; Trajectory hurts TB2 and MLGym. MTL beats ReasoningBank (+2.9) and AgentKB (+1.7) with 431 memories. Simple embedding retrieval beats reranking and rewriting. No significance tests

Distinguished formats and methods on average, with small differences (often 1 task in 100); some benchmarks show no or negative difference. Repeatability: three runs, Pass@3, no variance reported. Limitations of the method: none stated explicitly

No limitations section. Negative transfer (domain-mismatched anchoring, false validation confidence, misapplied best practices); need for better agentic memory retrieval and adaptation (domain routing, step-wise retrieval); cross-model transfer below self-generated memories; impact statement notes risk of unsafe code from misapplied patterns
